goal: Give the owner an **Ask withdrawal**: cancel ONE approved Ask's live **Outreach row** (`rendered`/`queued` -> `cancelled`/`owner_withdrawn`) in every **Batch state** where the **Halt latch** would cancel that row (`veto_window`, `approved`, `sending`), so one contact is lost instead of the whole cohort; withdrawing the last live row settles the batch through `closeBatchIfSettled` (**Settled batch**).
non_goals: Post-approval **Ask regeneration** in any form; no replacement row is ever inserted (ADR 0020 stands).
Releasing the withdrawn contact: no write to `solicitation_asks` (090 welds `status` to the decision) — the contact stays `over_contacted` for MIN_GAP_DAYS exactly like a halted ask.
Per-ask approval state, veto-deadline changes, or any `solicitation_batches` write other than what `closeBatchIfSettled` already performs.
Withdrawing a `sending` row (past the point of no return — halt's 'no further sends, not undo' contract) or undoing a withdrawal.
Showing withdrawn rows in the panel (they leave the list the way excluded rows do after approval); a countdown timer; copy changes to non-post-approval modes.
Admin/support withdrawal (#865 territory) and auto-lane special-casing (`approval_method` is not a gate, as for halt).
Analytics events, rate limits, or budgets for withdrawal (the approval lane emits none; withdrawal costs nothing).
The releaser (#630) itself — withdrawal only inherits the halt contract it must already honour.
user_visible_behavior: In the post-approval panel mode (`veto_window` / `approved` / `sending`) every listed row shows a `Withdraw` control; the first tap swaps it for an inline 'Withdraw this message?' [Withdraw] [Keep]; the second tap posts `{ batchId, askId }` to `POST /api/dashboard/solicitation/batch/withdraw`.
Success announces 'Withdrawn. N will send.' (N = live rows remaining) and refetches in place; the withdrawn row leaves the list.
Withdrawing the last live row settles the batch: the panel shows its existing settled mode.

Refusals: batch not withdrawable (409 with the derived state); the ask's current attempt is not live — `sending`/`sent`/`withheld`/`failed`/`unknown` or cancelled for another reason (409); a repeat withdrawal of an already-withdrawn ask is a 200 no-op; unknown batch or ask -> 404.
Post-approval panel copy gains one clause per state, e.g. veto_window: 'Approved. Nothing has left yet, and you can still stop this batch or withdraw a single message.'
Nothing changes before approval: the `built` mode keeps Ask exclusion + Ask regeneration and shows no Withdraw control.
invariants: Withdrawal only ever moves toward restraint: it cancels a row and never inserts, replaces or edits one — Owner approval's byte-for-byte guarantee is untouched.

Withdrawable states are exactly the halt-cancellable states of an approved batch: `veto_window`, `approved`, `sending`; refused in `pending`/`built`/`expired`/`halted`/`closed`. Row predicate `delivery_status IN ('rendered','queued')`, never `sending`.
Lock order B11 in ONE transaction: advisory batch lock -> `solicitation_batches` FOR UPDATE -> outreach UPDATE -> `recordStep` -> `closeBatchIfSettled`; no `agent_runs` lock before the spine call.
Every read and write is scoped by `account_id` + `business_id`; a foreign batch or ask is indistinguishable from an unknown one (`not_found`).
Validate before write: when the verb refuses, nothing has been written (postgres.js commits on a normal return).
`closeBatchIfSettled` stays the single terminal writer; withdrawal never stamps `send_closed_at` or the parent status itself.
`owner_withdrawn` is admitted by `solicitation_outreach_status_reason_consistency` only under `cancelled` (migration 109 re-spells 108's predicate verbatim plus that one value).
Server-authoritative: the refusal lives at the locked re-check, not in the UI; the route binds `requireSolicitationSendWriteAccess` (both flags), the same gate as halt.
Withdrawal writes no `solicitation_asks` row and none of the approval / veto columns on `solicitation_batches`.
edge_cases: Double-tap or stale tab: the ask's current attempt is already `cancelled`/`owner_withdrawn` -> `already_withdrawn`, 200, no step, no join, nothing written.
Row moved to `sending`/`sent` between render and click (future releaser) -> `not_live` carrying the status; nothing written.
Ask's current attempt is `withheld` (a pre-approval regeneration whose replacement was withheld) -> `not_live`; nothing to withdraw.
Ask id belongs to another batch of the same tenant, to another tenant, or does not exist -> `not_found`, indistinguishable.
Batch is `halted` (owner, admin or system) -> `not_withdrawable` with state `halted`; the batch lock serialises a concurrent halt and the loser sees the latch.
Batch is `built` (not yet approved) -> `not_withdrawable`; pre-approval deselection is Ask exclusion, and the panel never shows Withdraw there.
Last live row withdrawn -> `closeBatchIfSettled` closes the batch `exhausted`, records `send_batch_closed`, terminalizes the send parent `completed`; the response carries `closed: true`.
Auto-policy-approved batch (`approval_method='auto_policy'`) -> identical behaviour; there is no approval-method gate, as for halt.
Mixed-case batch or ask ids -> canonicalised once at entry (`agent_runs.subject_id` is a TEXT compare).
Concurrent releaser (#630, unwritten): withdrawal inherits halt's contract — the releaser re-checks the row under the batch lock before dispatch; a row already `sending` is never cancelled.
Body redaction: a withdrawn row is retention-eligible on the `rendered_at` clock like any cancelled row (092); no code change.
Two-tap confirm: one pending confirmation at a time — tapping Withdraw on another row moves it; Keep reverts; the control is disabled while any lane write is in flight.
